headline: Kokuyo's office-supplies site Kaunet says 300,525 customer records, mostly email addresses, leaked in the KARTE intrusion.
summary: Added s026, Kaunet's own Nov 24 second report (Tier 1, Japanese; plain reads are refused with HTTP 403, so it was read through a fetch tool and some characters were garbled; the figures and data types were legible). c013 now also covers Kaunet: 300,525 records (271,607 email addresses, 29,445 customer numbers, 25,492 phone numbers, overlapping); card numbers, expiry dates and login passwords not affected. Timeline t016. Re-read ZOZO's notice list (newest still Nov 20), PLAID's news list (newest still Nov 20), the KARTE status page (still Nov 19, restart date undecided) and the Personal Information Protection Commission's news page (nothing on this incident). No notice yet that PLAID began giving affected companies detailed data from Nov 24. c010 (attacker) stays Not established: no claim of responsibility in the press, no police or regulator attribution. A Nov 20 headline adding ZOZOTOWN and WEAR into 29.18 million is not used: ZOZO says the two overlap. No rumors with a factual claim found. Staleness check done: head still true.
author: Research agent

headline: GDO, Francfranc and CAMPFIRE each say millions of their own member records leaked or may have leaked via KARTE.
summary: No new ZOZO or PLAID notice since Nov 20 (both news pages checked; KARTE status page unchanged since Nov 19). Lead from the last run checked against the companies' own notices: added s023 GDO's notice, s024 Francfranc's notice (the site blocks automated reads, so its text was read through a search index) and s025 CAMPFIRE's second report, each Tier 1 and its own company. c013 stays Confirmed and now covers GDO (up to 6,974,506 records without names or emails), Francfranc (up to about 5.98 million member records with names, plus up to about 4 million purchase-history records) and CAMPFIRE (5,819,779 emails and hashed user IDs). New timeline rows t013 to t015. c009 stays Reported (vendor's own account), c010 attacker still Not established: no claim of responsibility reported in the press. No PPC or police statement found beyond companies saying they reported; PLAID says it will start giving affected companies detailed data from Nov 24. Staleness check done: head, known and not-known items still true. Privacy check done: no officials, staff or contact details named; help-desk lines, contact forms and press contacts left out.
